title: $\operatorname{Pic}$ is the divisor class group for smooth curves
statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth connected curve over $k$
(proper or not; for a disconnected smooth curve the assertion holds
componentwise). The map

$$
\operatorname{Cl}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C),\qquad
D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)],
$$

is an isomorphism of abelian groups (the group law on $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ being [lem-sc-pic-group]).

proof.text: Setting. By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], $C$ is a Noetherian integral scheme with generic point $\eta$ and function field $k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$; $\mathcal O_C(V)\subseteq\mathcal O_{C,x}\subseteq k(C)$ for nonempty open $V$ and $x\in V$; every point other than $\eta$ is closed and closed points exist; and for every closed point $P$, $\mathcal O_{C,P}$ is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $k(C)$ and normalized valuation $v_P$. Hence $\operatorname{div}(f)=\sum_Pv_P(f)[P]$ of [def-sc-divisor] is defined for $f\in k(C)^*$, and $v_P(fg)=v_P(f)+v_P(g)$ gives $\operatorname{div}(fg)=\operatorname{div}(f)+\operatorname{div}(g)$ and $\operatorname{div}(f^{-1})=-\operatorname{div}(f)$ (Stacks 02RP). So the principal divisors form a subgroup and $\operatorname{Cl}(C)=\operatorname{Div}(C)/\{\operatorname{div}f\}$ is an abelian group. By [lem-sc-divisor-module-local], for every $D\in\operatorname{Div}(C)$ the sheaf $\mathcal O_C(D)\subseteq k(C)$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], so $D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)]$ is a map $\operatorname{Div}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ [def-sc-picard-group].

source.place: Section 31.26 'Weil divisors' (section-Weil-divisors): Definition 0BE2, Lemma 02RP (divisors-lemma-div-additive), Definition 0BE4 (class group), exact sequence 0BE5; hypotheses of Lemma 0BE9

proof.text: The map factors through $\operatorname{Cl}(C)$. Let $D=\sum_Qn_Q[Q]$ and $f\in k(C)^*$, and put $D'=D+\operatorname{div}(f)$. For a nonempty open $V$ and $g\in k(C)^*$: $v_Q(gf^{-1})+n_Q+v_Q(f)=v_Q(g)+n_Q$ for every closed $Q\in V$, so $g\in\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$ if and only if $gf^{-1}\in\mathcal O_C(D')(V)$ (and $0\mapsto0$). Thus multiplication by $f^{-1}$ in $k(C)$ is a bijection $\mathcal O_C(D)(V)\to\mathcal O_C(D')(V)$, $\mathcal O_C(V)$-linear and compatible with restrictions (all sections are elements of the one field $k(C)$), with inverse multiplication by $f$; so $\mathcal O_C(D')=f^{-1}\mathcal O_C(D)\cong\mathcal O_C(D)$ and $[\mathcal O_C(D')]=[\mathcal O_C(D)]$. In particular ($D=0$, using $\mathcal O_C(0)=\mathcal O_C$ from [lem-sc-divisor-module-local]) $\mathcal O_C(\operatorname{div}f)=f^{-1}\mathcal O_C\cong\mathcal O_C$. Hence $D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)]$ induces a map $\phi:\operatorname{Cl}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence ('The map is well defined: ... $\mathcal O_C(\operatorname{div}f)=f^{-1}\mathcal O_C\cong\mathcal O_C$'); cf. Stacks Divisors Lemma 02SH (divisors-lemma-divisor-meromorphic-well-defined)

proof.text: $\phi$ is a homomorphism. Let $D=\sum n_Q[Q]$, $D'=\sum n'_Q[Q]$. For a nonempty open $V$, $g\in\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$, $h\in\mathcal O_C(D')(V)$ (both nonzero) we have $v_Q(gh)+n_Q+n'_Q=(v_Q(g)+n_Q)+(v_Q(h)+n'_Q)\ge0$ for closed $Q\in V$, so $gh\in\mathcal O_C(D+D')(V)$. The product $(g,h)\mapsto gh$ is $\mathcal O_C(V)$-bilinear and compatible with restrictions, hence induces (universal property of the tensor product of $\mathcal O_C$-modules, the sheafification of the presheaf tensor product) an $\mathcal O_C$-linear map $\mu:\mathcal O_C(D)\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal O_C(D')\to\mathcal O_C(D+D')$. It is an isomorphism, which may be checked on an open cover. Let $P$ be a closed point and $t$ a uniformizer of $\mathcal O_{C,P}$; [lem-sc-divisor-module-local] applied to $D$, $D'$, $D+D'$ with the same $t$ gives neighbourhoods whose intersection $U\ni P$ satisfies $\mathcal O_C(D)|_U=t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_U$, $\mathcal O_C(D')|_U=t^{-n'_P}\mathcal O_U$, $\mathcal O_C(D+D')|_U=t^{-n_P-n'_P}\mathcal O_U$. Under the isomorphisms $a\mapsto t^{-n_P}a$, $b\mapsto t^{-n'_P}b$, $c\mapsto t^{-n_P-n'_P}c$ from $\mathcal O_U$, $\mu|_U$ becomes the multiplication $\mathcal O_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_U$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, an isomorphism. These $U$ cover $C$: they cover the closed points, and $\eta$ lies in every nonempty open ([lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]: every point is closed or $\eta$, and a closed point exists). So $\mu$ is an isomorphism and $\phi([D+D'])=\phi([D])\cdot\phi([D'])$ for the group law of $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ given by $\otimes$ [lem-sc-pic-group], [def-sc-picard-group].

source.place: ## Proof, second sentence ('It is a homomorphism: the multiplication map ... is an isomorphism (locally both sides are invertible modules generated by the same element of $k(C)$)'); cf. Stacks Divisors Lemma 02SL (divisors-lemma-c1-additive)

proof.text: $\phi$ is surjective. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module. $C$ is an integral curve over $k$ ([lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]), so by [lem-sc-line-bundle-rational-section] $\mathcal L$ has a nonzero rational section $s$ and $f\mapsto fs$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_C(\operatorname{div}s)\to\mathcal L$. Hence $[\mathcal L]=\phi([\operatorname{div}s])$.

proof.text: Conclusion. By steps 2 and 3, $\phi:\operatorname{Cl}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$, $[D]\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)]$, is a well-defined homomorphism of abelian groups; by step 5 its kernel (the classes $[D]$ with $\mathcal O_C(D)\cong\mathcal O_C$, the unit of $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$) is trivial, so it is injective; by step 4 it is surjective. Hence it is an isomorphism.
